t: There are hereby authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary, but not more than $17,000,000, for the acquisition of lands and interests in land under the provisions of this Act.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations of up to $17,000,000 for acquiring land. A tempting reading is that land acquisition implies dealings with outside landowners, but the text sets out no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision here.
fable.s: There are hereby authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary, but not more than $17,000,000, for the acquisition of lands and interests in land under the provisions of this Act.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard authorization of appropriations clause. It merely sets a funding limit for the government to acquire land. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements for outside input mentioned.
qwen_block.s: There are hereby authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary, but not more than $17,000,000, for the acquisition of lands and interests in land under the provisions of this Act.

opus.w: This provision only authorizes funding, capped at $17,000,000, for buying land. It does not require or allow any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government. Buying land may affect landowners, but the text gives no one outside the government a role in the decision.
opus.s: There are hereby authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary, but not more than $17,000,000, for the acquisition of lands and interests in land under the provisions of this Act.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriation authorization for land acquisition. It does not contain any language requiring consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public) before a decision is made. The act of acquiring land is an administrative/executive action, not a participatory process as defined.
qwen_chat.s: There are hereby authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary, but not more than $17,000,000, for the acquisition of lands and interests in land under the provisions of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "acquisition of lands" implies negotiation with private landowners, which is a form of participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses, and generally treats standard government procurement or land acquisition as administrative actions rather than the specific type of consultative participation defined (e.g., advisory boards, public comment, consultation with states/tribes before a decision). The text itself contains no language requiring consultation, hearings, or input from outside parties; it is purely an appropriation authorization.
